ei.title: Breaking the Cycle: Solutions to E-waste
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: On her way to a study group meeting, Liz accidentally dropped her laptop on the street, seriously damaging it. Although it still turns on, the screen is cracked, and some keys are not working. She can have it repaired, but she is hesitating to do so. Sometimes repairs are expensive, and they often take a long time. Besides, the laptop is about five years old. In this case, getting rid of the old one and purchasing a new one might seem like a more reasonable option. In reality, however, it may not be the best thing to do. If Liz throws her laptop in the trash, she will be contributing to a serious problem: e-waste. What exactly is e-waste? The term refers to discarded electronic devices and electrical appliances. Due to toxic materials contained in these products, such as lead, e-waste is a serious health and environmental hazard. To make matters worse, the amount of e-waste produced each year is increasing at an alarming rate. In 2021, a total of 57.4 million metric tons* of e-waste was generated worldwide, which was a 37% increase from 2014, the year when data about e-waste was first collected. Experts predict that by 2030, the amount of e-waste generated annually will have doubled in just 16 years. For this reason, efforts are being made to address this problem, most of which are focused on making products easier to repair. Let’s take a look at some practical approaches from around the world. Right-to-Repair Movement: Empowering Consumers One reason many people dispose of their damaged devices is that they are too difficult to repair. For example, a device may be difficult to disassemble, or its manufacturer may require that it be brought to an official service center to be fixed. Many companies do not allow their customers to take their damaged items to third-party repair shops. What is more, some products are intentionally designed to be difficult to repair. It is common for consumers to be unable to acquire the instructions for how to fix their items or the parts needed to complete repairs. The right-to-repair movement is trying to solve these problems by promoting legislation that states the following: If you own a product, you have the right to fix it yourself or bring it to a technician of your choice. To protect the rights of consumers, the right-to-repair movement demands four things. First, companies must make information about their products available to everyone. Second, third parties, including individuals, should be able to obtain the parts and tools required to make repairs. Third, the practice of preventing consumers from installing custom software on their own devices should be prohibited by law. Finally, it demands that manufacturers design devices in a way that makes repairs as easy as possible. Advocates of the movement say that if all these goals are accomplished, far less e-waste will be generated. Thanks to their efforts, more than 40 states in the U.S. have begun working on right-to-repair legislation. This movement is gaining a growing influence in Europe as well, with more and more countries joining the cause. Repairability Index: Information at a Glance In January 2021, the French government passed a bill that requires that every manufacturer include a “repairability index” on five categories of electronic devices and electrical appliances: smartphones, laptops, washing machines, televisions, and lawn mowers. Using a score ranging from 0 to 10, as well as a color-coded system, the index lets consumers see how easily the product can be repaired before they purchase it. The index takes into account several elements, including the availability of repair information, the ease of disassembly, and the price of spare parts. A low number on a bright red label means that repairing the product will be difficult, whereas a high number on a green label indicates that the product is easy to repair. The index was designed to have two positive effects. Firstly, it allows consumers to make informed decisions when purchasing new devices and appliances. Secondly, it encourages manufacturers to make their products easier to repair. As a result, with fewer electronic and electrical items ending up in its landfills, France can expect to make a transition to a more sustainable society in the near future. The impact of the index, however, is likely to spread far beyond France. We live in a global economy, and any company that wants to sell its appliances on the French market will need to label its products according to the repairability index. If the index is successful, we can anticipate seeing more countries around the world following France’s innovative lead. Repair Cafés: It Takes a Community When consumers are given the right tools and materials, along with some helpful advice, they can repair much of the damage that occurs to electronic products by themselves. That is why Repair Cafés were started. They are free meeting places where people can gather together and fix their broken devices. The cafés are staffed by volunteer experts who can give technical advice and teach people how to fix things. The first Repair Café was opened in the Netherlands in the city of Amsterdam in 2009. It was such a success that the idea soon spread to neighboring countries. Before long, there were Repair Cafés in over 30 countries around the world. Along with preventing damaged items from becoming e-waste, these cafés also encourage people to share their invaluable skills and knowledge about the repair and maintenance of electronics. They continue to grow in popularity, with more and more people signing up to volunteer. By providing spaces where people can learn, Repair Cafés enable individuals to maintain their devices and extend their life spans. Furthermore, they foster a sustainable perspective that can have a huge positive impact on our future. Do you remember Liz, the girl who dropped her laptop? Imagine she lived in a world where repairing damaged devices and appliances was simply part of everyday life. If that were the case, her options wouldn’t be limited to paying for expensive repairs or throwing away her laptop and buying a new one. She would be able to order the necessary parts online and replace them herself. Alternatively, she could bring her damaged device to the nearest Repair Café to get advice on how to fix it. Repairing it probably wouldn’t be very hard, as she likely would have purchased a laptop with a high repairability score. In fact, this sustainable world is a future we can all enjoy if we work toward it together. Even more importantly, it is a future in which people will generate far less e-waste, making our planet a cleaner, healthier place for everyone.

questions.passage: On her way to a study group meeting, Liz accidentally dropped her laptop on the street, seriously (A)[damaging / fixing] it. Although it still turns on, the screen is cracked, and some keys are not working. She can have it repaired, but she is hesitating to do so. Sometimes repairs are (B)[expensive / cheap], and they often take a long time. Besides, the laptop is about five years old. In this case, getting rid of the old one and purchasing a new one might seem like a more (C)[foolish / reasonable] option. In reality, however, it may not be the best thing to do.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① damaging(손상시키는)+expensive(비싼)+reasonable(합리적인): 노트북을 떨어뜨려 '심각하게 손상시켰고', 수리 작업은 '비싸며', 그래서 새것을 사는 게 더 '합리적인' 선택처럼 보인다는 문맥에 모두 맞음 ← 정답
❌ ② fixing(고치는)은 'seriously damaging it(심각하게 손상시키다)'과 반대
❌ ③ cheap(값싼)은 '수리가 비싸다'는 흐름과 반대
❌ ④ foolish(어리석은)는 'a more reasonable option(더 합리적인 선택)'과 반대
det.tip: damaging=손상시키는, expensive=비싼, reasonable=합리적인

questions.passage: What exactly is e-waste? The term refers to (A)[discarded / collected] electronic devices and electrical appliances. Due to (B)[toxic / harmless] materials contained in these products, such as lead, e-waste is a serious health and environmental hazard. To make matters worse, the amount of e-waste produced each year is increasing at an alarming rate. In 2021, a total of 57.4 million metric tons* of e-waste was generated worldwide, which was a 37% increase from 2014, the year when data about e-waste was first collected. Experts predict that by 2030, the amount of e-waste generated annually will have (C)[halved / doubled] in just 16 years. For this reason, efforts are being made to address this problem, most of which are focused on making products easier to repair. Let’s take a look at some practical approaches from around the world.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① collected(수집된)는 전자 쓰레기가 '버려진(discarded)' 장치라는 문맥과 반대
✅ ② discarded(버려진)+toxic(유독성의)+doubled(두 배가 된): 전자 쓰레기는 '버려진' 장치를 가리키고, '유독성' 물질 때문에 위험하며, 2030년에 그 양이 '두 배가 될' 것이라는 문맥에 맞음 ← 정답
❌ ③ harmless(무해한)는 '유독성 물질 때문에 위험하다'는 흐름과 반대
❌ ④ halved(반으로 준)는 양이 '두 배가 된다'는 예측과 반대
det.tip: discarded=버려진, toxic=유독성의, doubled=두 배가 된

questions.passage: As a result, with (A)[fewer / more] electronic and electrical items ending up in its landfills, France can expect to make a (B)[transition / return] to a more sustainable society in the near future. The impact of the index, however, is likely to spread far beyond France. We live in a global economy, and any company that wants to sell its appliances on the French market will need to label its products according to the repairability index. If the index is successful, we can anticipate seeing more countries around the world following France’s (C)[outdated / innovative] lead. Repair Cafés: It Takes a Community When consumers are given the right tools and materials, along with some helpful advice, they can repair much of the damage that occurs to electronic products by themselves. That is why Repair Cafés were started.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① more(더 많은)는 '더 적은(fewer)' 제품이 매립지에 간다는 문맥과 반대
❌ ② return(복귀)은 더 지속 가능한 사회로의 '변화(transition)'라는 문맥과 어긋남
❌ ③ outdated(구식의)는 프랑스의 '혁신적인(innovative)' 선례라는 문맥과 반대
✅ ④ fewer(더 적은)+transition(변화)+innovative(혁신적인): 지수 덕분에 '더 적은' 제품이 매립지에 가고, 프랑스가 지속 가능한 사회로 '변화'할 것이며, 다른 나라가 프랑스의 '혁신적인' 선례를 따를 것이라는 문맥에 맞음 ← 정답
det.tip: fewer=더 적은, transition=변화, innovative=혁신적인

questions.passage: What exactly is e-waste? The term refers to ①<u>discarded</u> electronic devices and electrical appliances. Due to ②<u>toxic</u> materials contained in these products, such as lead, e-waste is a serious health and environmental ③<u>benefit</u>. To make matters worse, the amount of e-waste produced each year is increasing at an ④<u>alarming</u> rate. In 2021, a total of 57.4 million metric tons* of e-waste was generated worldwide, which was a 37% increase from 2014, the year when data about e-waste was first collected. Experts predict that by 2030, the amount of e-waste generated annually will have doubled in just 16 years. For this reason, efforts are being made to address this problem, most of which are focused on making products easier to repair. Let’s take a look at some practical approaches from around the world.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ benefit → hazard: 유독성 물질 때문에 전자 쓰레기는 심각한 '위험 요소(hazard)'이다
det.analysis:
✅ ① discarded: 전자 쓰레기는 '버려진(discarded)' 장치를 가리킨다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ② toxic: 납과 같은 '유독성(toxic)' 물질이라는 문맥에 적절
❌ ③ benefit(이익) → hazard(위험 요소): 'a serious health and environmental hazard'에서 유독성 물질 때문에 전자 쓰레기가 건강·환경에 심각한 '위험 요소'라는 뜻이므로 hazard가 맞다. benefit은 정반대 ← 정답
✅ ④ alarming: 전자 쓰레기 양이 '걱정스러운(alarming)' 속도로 증가한다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: hazard(위험 요소) ↔ benefit(이익)

questions.passage: Right-to-Repair Movement: Empowering Consumers One reason many people ①<u>keep</u> of their damaged devices is that they are too difficult to repair. For example, a device may be difficult to ②<u>disassemble</u>, or its manufacturer may require that it be brought to an official service center to be fixed. Many companies do not allow their customers to take their damaged items to third-party repair shops. What is more, some products are ③<u>intentionally</u> designed to be difficult to repair. It is common for consumers to be unable to ④<u>acquire</u> the instructions for how to fix their items or the parts needed to complete repairs.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① keep → dispose: 많은 사람이 고장 난 장치를 '버리는(dispose of)' 이유
det.analysis:
❌ ① keep(보관하다) → dispose(버리다): 'many people dispose of their damaged devices'에서 사람들이 고장 난 장치를 '버린다'는 뜻이므로 dispose가 맞다. keep은 정반대 ← 정답
✅ ② disassemble: 장치를 '분해하기(disassemble)' 어렵다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ③ intentionally: 몇몇 제품은 '의도적으로(intentionally)' 수리하기 어렵게 만들어진다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ④ acquire: 설명서나 부품을 '얻지(acquire)' 못한다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: dispose of(버리다) ↔ keep(보관하다)

questions.passage: To protect the rights of consumers, the right-to-repair movement demands four things. First, companies must make information about their products ①<u>available</u> to everyone. Second, third parties, including individuals, should be able to obtain the parts and tools ②<u>required</u> to make repairs. Third, the practice of preventing consumers from installing custom software on their own devices should be ③<u>allowed</u> by law. Finally, it demands that manufacturers design devices in a way that makes repairs as easy as possible. Advocates of the movement say that if all these goals are ④<u>accomplished</u>, far less e-waste will be generated.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ allowed → prohibited: 맞춤형 소프트웨어 설치를 막는 행위는 법으로 '금지되어야(prohibited)' 한다
det.analysis:
✅ ① available: 제품 정보를 모두가 '이용할 수 있게(available)' 해야 한다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ② required: 수리에 '필요한(required)' 부품과 도구라는 문맥에 적절
❌ ③ allowed(허용되다) → prohibited(금지되다): 'the practice of preventing consumers from installing custom software ... should be prohibited by law'에서 소비자가 소프트웨어를 설치하지 못하게 하는 행위가 법으로 '금지되어야' 한다는 뜻이므로 prohibited가 맞다. allowed는 정반대 ← 정답
✅ ④ accomplished: 모든 목표가 '이루어지면(accomplished)' 전자 쓰레기가 줄어든다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: prohibited(금지되다) ↔ allowed(허용되다)

Repairing it probably wouldn’t be very hard, as she likely would have purchased a laptop with a high repairability score. In fact, this sustainable world is a future we can all enjoy if we work toward it together. Even more importantly, it is a future in which people will generate far less e-waste, making our planet a cleaner, healthier place for everyone.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 necessary와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① unnecessary: 불필요한 ← 정답
❌ ② essential: 필수적인 (유의어라 반대 아님)
❌ ③ required: 요구되는 (유의어라 반대 아님)
❌ ④ vital: 매우 중요한 (유의어라 반대 아님)
det.tip: order the necessary parts(필요한 부품) ↔ unnecessary(불필요한)

questions.passage:
(A) E-waste contains toxic materials, such as <u>lead</u>, which can seriously harm both human health and the surrounding environment. For this reason, old electronic products must never be thrown away carelessly.
(B) If the repairability index proves successful in France, many other nations may follow France's innovative <u>lead</u> and adopt similar labeling rules for their own markets.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B) 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 lead의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① (A)의 lead는 유독성 금속인 '납'을 뜻하고(toxic materials such as lead=납과 같은 유독성 물질), (B)의 lead는 다른 나라가 따르는 '선례·주도'를 뜻함(follow France's innovative lead=프랑스의 혁신적인 선례를 따르다) ← 정답
❌ ② (A)는 '선례'가 아니라 '납'임
❌ ③ (A)는 '이끌다'(동사)가 아니라 '납'(명사)임
❌ ④ (B)는 '이끌다'가 아니라 '선례'임
det.tip: lead: (A) 납(금속) / (B) 선례·주도

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"to take something apart into its separate pieces"

det.analysis:
❌ ① purchase(구입하다): 물건을 사다
❌ ② generate(발생시키다): 무언가를 만들어 내다
✅ ③ disassemble(분해하다): 어떤 것을 여러 부분으로 따로 떼어 내다 ← 정답
❌ ④ replace(교체하다): 다른 것으로 바꾸다
det.tip: a device may be difficult to disassemble = 분해하기 어렵다 → disassemble = 분해하다

questions.passage: Along with __________ (prevent) damaged items from becoming e-waste, these cafés also encourage people to share their skills and knowledge about the repair of electronics. By doing so, they foster a sustainable perspective about our future.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: prevent(동사 원형) → preventing: 앞에 전치사 'Along with'가 있으므로 전치사의 목적어 자리에는 동명사가 와야 한다. 따라서 preventing으로 바꿔야 한다. 'Along with preventing ~(~을 막는 것과 더불어)'로 해석한다.
det.tip: 전치사(Along with) + 동명사(preventing): ~을 막는 것과 더불어

questions.passage: When consumers are given the right tools and materials, they can repair much of the damage that __________ (occur) to electronic products by themselves. That is why Repair Cafés were started.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: occur(동사 원형) → occurs: 관계대명사 that이 가리키는 선행사가 'the damage(단수)'이므로, 관계대명사절 안의 동사는 선행사에 수를 맞춰 3인칭 단수 현재형 occurs가 되어야 한다. 'the damage that occurs(발생하는 손상)'로 해석한다.
det.tip: 선행사 the damage(단수) → 관계사절 동사 occurs

questions.passage: Firstly, it allows consumers to make __________ when purchasing new devices and appliances. Secondly, it encourages manufacturers to make their products easier to repair. As a result, with fewer electronic and electrical items ending up in its landfills, France can expect to make a transition to a more sustainable society in the near future. The impact of the index, however, is likely to spread far beyond France. We live in a global economy, and any company that wants to sell its appliances on the French market will need to label its products according to the repairability index. If the index is successful, we can anticipate seeing more countries around the world following France’s innovative lead. Repair Cafés: It Takes a Community When consumers are given the right tools and materials, along with some helpful advice, they can repair much of the damage that occurs to electronic products by themselves. That is why Repair Cafés were started.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① random guesses(무작위 추측): 지수가 주는 정보 활용과 반대
❌ ② quick profits(빠른 이익): 소비자의 구매 결정과 무관
❌ ③ final payments(최종 지불): 문맥과 관련 없음
✅ ④ informed decisions(정보에 근거한 결정): 지수가 소비자들이 새 제품을 살 때 '정보에 근거한 결정'을 내리게 한다는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답
det.tip: make informed decisions: 정보에 근거한 결정을 내리다

questions.passage: Furthermore, they foster __________ that can have a huge positive impact on our future. Do you remember Liz, the girl who dropped her laptop? Imagine she lived in a world where repairing damaged devices and appliances was simply part of everyday life. If that were the case, her options wouldn’t be limited to paying for expensive repairs or throwing away her laptop and buying a new one. She would be able to order the necessary parts online and replace them herself. Alternatively, she could bring her damaged device to the nearest Repair Café to get advice on how to fix it. Repairing it probably wouldn’t be very hard, as she likely would have purchased a laptop with a high repairability score. In fact, this sustainable world is a future we can all enjoy if we work toward it together. Even more importantly, it is a future in which people will generate far less e-waste, making our planet a cleaner, healthier place for everyone.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 a sustainable perspective(지속 가능한 관점)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① a quick profit(빠른 이익): 수리 카페가 추구하는 가치와 다름
✅ ② a sustainable perspective(지속 가능한 관점): 수리 카페가 우리 미래에 막대한 긍정적 영향을 미칠 '지속 가능한 관점'을 조성한다는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답
❌ ③ a strict rule(엄격한 규칙): 본문 흐름과 무관
❌ ④ a negative attitude(부정적인 태도): '긍정적 영향'이라는 흐름과 반대
det.tip: foster a sustainable perspective: 지속 가능한 관점을 조성하다
